<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-summary">Summary</button></h2><div id="work-acc-summary" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Mahāvīrasvāmīstotra&quot; is a Sanskrit hymn dedicated to Lord Mahāvīra, the founder of Jainism. It is a devotional poem that praises Lord Mahāvīra's life, teachings, and virtues. The hymn comprises of 44 verses, each highlighting a different aspect of Lord Mahāvīra's life and teachings. It describes his birth, his renunciation of the world, his rigorous spiritual practices, and his attainment of enlightenment. The hymn also praises his compassion, wisdom, and his role in the propagation of Jainism. &quot;Mahāvīrasvāmīstotra&quot; is considered one of the most significant works of Hemacandra, and it has been widely studied and recited by Jains for centuries. The hymn not only celebrates Lord Mahāvīra's life but also serves as an inspiration for Jains to follow in his footsteps and strive towards spiritual purity and enlightenment.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contents">Contents</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contents" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">&quot;Mahāvīrasvāmīstotra&quot; comprises 44 verses, each of which highlights a different aspect of Lord Mahāvīra's life, teachings, and virtues. Here is a brief overview of the contents of the hymn:<br>Verses 1-7: These verses praise Lord Mahāvīra's birth and his noble qualities, such as his compassion, wisdom, and purity.<br>Verses 8-12: These verses describe Lord Mahāvīra's renunciation of the world and his rigorous spiritual practices.<br>Verses 13-17: These verses highlight Lord Mahāvīra's attainment of enlightenment and his role as a spiritual teacher.<br>Verses 18-22: These verses describe Lord Mahāvīra's teachings, including his emphasis on non-violence, truth, and self-control.<br>Verses 23-28: These verses praise Lord Mahāvīra's virtues, such as his equanimity, humility, and detachment.<br>Verses 29-32: These verses describe the benefits of following Lord Mahāvīra's teachings, such as liberation from worldly suffering and the attainment of spiritual bliss.<br>Verses 33-36: These verses highlight Lord Mahāvīra's role in the propagation of Jainism and the spread of his teachings.<br>Verses 37-40: These verses describe the power of Lord Mahāvīra's name and the benefits of reciting his hymn.<br>Verses 41-44: These verses offer a final prayer to Lord Mahāvīra, asking for his blessings and guidance on the path towards spiritual liberation.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-uniqueness">Uniqueness</button></h2><div id="work-acc-uniqueness" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">&quot;Mahāvīrasvāmīstotra&quot; is a unique work in several ways. Firstly, it is one of the most important and widely-recited hymns in Jainism, and is considered a key devotional text in the Jain canon. It is a powerful expression of devotion to Lord Mahāvīra, and highlights his many virtues and achievements. Secondly, the hymn is notable for its poetic beauty and literary excellence. Hemacandra was a highly-skilled poet, and &quot;Mahāvīrasvāmīstotra&quot; is a masterpiece of Sanskrit literature. The verses are crafted with great skill and care, and use a range of poetic devices to create a powerful and moving effect. Finally, &quot;Mahāvīrasvāmīstotra&quot; is unique in its ability to convey complex philosophical and spiritual ideas in a simple and accessible way. The hymn covers a wide range of themes, including non-violence, detachment, and the attainment of spiritual liberation. Despite the depth and complexity of these ideas, the hymn is written in clear and simple language, making it accessible to a wide range of readers.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contribution">Contribution &amp; Notes</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contribution" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">&quot;Mahāvīrasvāmīstotra&quot; is a highly significant work in the history of Sanskrit literature. As a devotional hymn, it occupies a prominent place in the canon of Jain literature and is widely recited by devotees. However, its literary and philosophical contributions cannot be overlooked. The hymn showcases Hemacandra's mastery over the Sanskrit language and his skill as a poet. The verses are crafted with great care, using a range of literary devices such as alliteration, metaphor, and simile to create a powerful and evocative effect. The language is rich, flowing, and highly expressive, making it a joy to read and recite. &quot;Mahāvīrasvāmīstotra&quot; contributes to the philosophical and spiritual tradition of Sanskrit literature. The hymn emphasizes the central tenets of Jainism, such as non-violence, detachment, and spiritual liberation, and presents these ideas in a clear and accessible way. It also highlights the virtues of Lord Mahāvīra, portraying him as the embodiment of these ideals.<br><br>&quot;Mahāvīrasvāmīstotra&quot; is a significant Jain hymn in Sanskrit that praises Lord Mahāvīra, the last Tīrthaṅkara of Jainism. It is considered one of the most important Jain texts and is often recited during Jain festivals and religious ceremonies. One notable aspect of the &quot;Mahāvīrasvāmīstotra&quot; is its emphasis on Lord Mahāvīra's divinity. While Jainism is typically considered a non-theistic religion, the hymn portrays Lord Mahāvīra as a divine being worthy of worship and devotion. This reflects the evolving nature of Jainism over time, as it became more institutionalized and began to incorporate elements of traditional Indian religious practices.</div></div></div>
